Marissa / Karthik,

Quick thread — Theraplane (pilot → enterprise) got a last-minute ask from their CFO for an aggressive billing concession to make the economics work for an expanded pilot. Key points: 
- They want a time-bound rebate applied to month-1 invoices that would effectively offset onboarding/setup costs (one-time).
- Proposed structure: 30% rebate on first-month charges up to $150k, with a 12-month minimum commitment and a 6-month clawback if they churn early.
- Rationale in attached forecast (low-risk: heavy signal for multi-product expansion in Q2 of next year).

I understand this is outside standard guardrails — asking for VP/CFO sign-off as an exception. Attaching the forecast and a quick precedent matrix I pulled (theraplane_forecast_v3.pdf, precedent_matrix.xlsx).

Next steps I recommend: 
1) Confirm internal appetite for a one-off rebate + clawback (legal will want explicit language).
2) If yes, get Marissa + Karthik to route to finance for VP/CFO memo.
3) If approved, I’ll send an updated MOU to their legal for signature.

Customer note (Elliot) — they’re on a compressed timeline and asked if we can surface a commercial exception today so they can include it in their renewal committee on Monday.

Thanks,
Ben

Marissa, Karthik —

Appended business case below (short). I’ve pulled examples in the precedent matrix where we approved one-time onboarding rebates tied to expansion in verticals with long sales cycles — highlighted rows 2 and 5 (see attached).

Business case (summary): Theraplane is a connected devices vendor with a targeted enterprise expansion plan. They have two active pilots with strong technical success; the CFO is willing to commit to a 12-month paid contract if we remove the onboarding cost friction for month-1. The rebate reduces initial ARR recognition but materially increases conversion probability to multi-region deployment (estimated +$1.6M ARR over 24 months). Worst-case impact: a $45k net revenue deferral over the first quarter (with clawback provision recovering ~70% if they cancel within 6 months).

Commercial ask: one-time 30% rebate capped at $150k on month-1 invoice, 12-month minimum commitment, 6-month prorated clawback. Legal will need a tight MOU; I can run the draft once I have internal signoff.

Elliot — flagging that we need this by COB Monday to make your renewal committee. If you have an internal champion who can email a short note to their CFO (naming who will approve internally), that will help speed sign-off.

Ben

Attachments: theraplane_forecast_v3.pdf; precedent_matrix.xlsx; (I can produce a one-page MOU draft if we get greenlight)

--- BEGIN EXCEPTION MEMO (draft) ---
Subject: Commercial exception request — one-time onboarding rebate for Theraplane (Deal DL-6789)
Requested by: Ben Carter, AE
Customer: Theraplane (pilot -> enterprise expansion)
Ask: Approve a one-time 30% rebate on month-1 charges, capped at $150,000. Conditioned on: signed 12-month minimum commitment, 6-month prorated clawback.
Business rationale: Product-validated pilots with demonstrable ROI; accelerated expansion to additional product lines expected to generate incremental ARR estimated at $1.6M over 24 months. Rebate reduces friction for CFO signoff in current renewal committee.
Risks: Short-term revenue deferral of up to $150k, with partial recovery via clawback; sets a precedent for onboarding concessions in the devices vertical.
Recommended approval path: CFO approval required for one-off rebate > $100k. VP Commercial sign-off sufficient for rebates <= $100k.
Required next steps: Legal to produce a short MOU with clawback language; Finance to confirm GAAP treatment and revenue recognition path; Deal Desk to prepare final commercial sheet and DocuSign package.
--- END EXCEPTION MEMO ---

I have attached a quick precedent matrix and a proposed MOU one-pager (mou_onepager_signed_draft.docx). My recommendation: route to CFO with Marissa’s note endorsing the strategic expansion (Marissa, if you’re good with the memo, I will attach it to the finance ticket).

If finance okays, I’ll push the DocuSign by EOD Monday.
